account: UC San Diego Health evaluated COMPOSER in two emergency departments among 6,217 adults with sepsis. The model went live on 7 December 2022, with follow-up through 30 April 2023. Post-deployment mortality was 9.49%, compared with a modeled counterfactual of 11.39%: an adjusted reduction of 1.9 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.3–3.5). Raw pre-deployment mortality was 10.3%. The estimated benefit was statistically significant at one hospital and not the other. The study used historical controls, without randomization or a concurrent untreated group. The COMPOSER team published the evaluation in npj Digital Medicine on 23 January 2024. In an npj Digital Medicine editorial of 1 March 2024, authors from the University of Toronto and Harvard Medical School accepted the reported association and noted that the benefit appeared at one of the two hospitals. On 12 June 2024 the COMPOSER team published an author correction that restored the study's missing Table 3. A meta-analysis by Yale authors, published on 13 May 2025, pooled seven randomized trials of other sepsis alert systems and found no significant effect on mortality. That meta-analysis did not include the COMPOSER study, which was not randomized. The COMPOSER team reported in August 2026 that the alerts were still in use in both emergency departments through October 2025. A large language model layer was added to the alerts in July 2024.

fields.account: UC San Diego Health evaluated COMPOSER in two emergency departments among 6,217 adults with sepsis. The model went live on 7 December 2022, with follow-up through 30 April 2023. Post-deployment mortality was 9.49%, compared with a modeled counterfactual of 11.39%: an adjusted reduction of 1.9 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.3–3.5). Raw pre-deployment mortality was 10.3%. The estimated benefit was statistically significant at one hospital and not the other. The study used historical controls, without randomization or a concurrent untreated group. The COMPOSER team published the evaluation in npj Digital Medicine on 23 January 2024. In an npj Digital Medicine editorial of 1 March 2024, authors from the University of Toronto and Harvard Medical School accepted the reported association and noted that the benefit appeared at one of the two hospitals. On 12 June 2024 the COMPOSER team published an author correction that restored the study's missing Table 3. A meta-analysis by Yale authors, published on 13 May 2025, pooled seven randomized trials of other sepsis alert systems and found no significant effect on mortality. That meta-analysis did not include the COMPOSER study, which was not randomized. The COMPOSER team reported in August 2026 that the alerts were still in use in both emergency departments through October 2025. A large language model layer was added to the alerts in July 2024.
